beats.text: Cube shaped filters. Cylinder shaped socket.
beats.note: The command module used cubic lithium hydroxide canisters to scrub carbon dioxide. The lunar module used cylindrical ones and had no backups, says Space Center Houston.

beats.text: The lander was built for two people.
beats.note: HobbySpace says it was designed for two people for 36 hours, not three people for 96.

beats.text: About 1am, four hours after the explosion.
beats.note: Crew systems chief Ed Smylie realised then that carbon dioxide had to be dealt with, according to collectSPACE via Space.com.

beats.name: Ed Smylie
beats.role: Chief of NASA's crew systems division. He said probably 60 people were involved.

beats.text: A hose, a sock, a plastic bag, cue cards and duct tape.
beats.note: That is the Space.com list. HobbySpace adds a flight manual cover. Accounts differ on the exact parts.

beats.text: The crew called it the mail box.
beats.note: NASA's caption reads: Apollo 13 Crew Installing 'Mail Box' for Purging Carbon Dioxide From Lunar Module, April 14, 1970.

beats.text: Houston could not send pictures. It talked the crew through it.
